NDT training in Calgary: how it works for Calgary employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training for Calgary employers and technicians. Theory runs live online, and practicals run onsite at your facility. Level I, II and III courses cover UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET under ASNT Level III oversight. It fits Calgary companies whose clients, contracts or codes call for SNT-TC-1A, which usually means US-headquartered owners, cross-border work and US-code fabrication. It is not a substitute for Canada's national CGSB (ISO 9712) certification.

The distinction above is the most important thing on this page. In Canada, the national NDT personnel certification scheme is CAN/CGSB-48.9712, Canada's adoption of ISO 9712. It is a third-party, central certification administered federally. Many Alberta owners, inspection companies and regulators' customers expect technicians to hold it. SNT-TC-1A works differently. It is an employer-based system in which the employer's written practice governs training, experience and examinations, and the employer certifies its own people. Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based. We do not offer CGSB certification, we do not claim that our training counts toward it, and we will not suggest that ASNT certification replaces it where a Canadian contract calls for CGSB.

So who is this page for? Calgary is the head-office city of the Canadian energy industry, and much of the work its companies manage has a US side. There are US-owned operators and their Canadian subsidiaries, pipelines that cross the border, modules and pressure equipment fabricated in Alberta for US projects, and inspection companies that send crews south to US refineries and pipelines. Where the contract, the client's specification or a US code (ASME, API 1104, AWS) calls for SNT-TC-1A-qualified personnel, the employer needs a written practice and trained, examined technicians. That is the gap we fill.

As on every Atlantis city page, we are explicit: Atlantis has no training centre in Calgary. Theory is delivered live online, and practical training and exams take place onsite at your facility under ASNT Level III oversight. If you need that for your team, request a Calgary training quote. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Calgary

All courses are built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Recommended hours by method and level are in our training-requirements matrix. The employer's written practice sets the figures that actually apply. These hours are SNT-TC-1A figures and are not the same as CGSB requirements.

MethodLevelsWhat Calgary employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (ultrasonic)I, II, III prepThickness and corrosion surveys on gas-plant and in-situ oil-sands facility piping; weld examination on US-code pressure equipment and modules; pipeline integrity digsNone for Level I; Level I plus documented experience for Level II
PAUT (phased array)II, III prepEncoded girth-weld examination on pipeline construction, weld inspection on module and spool fabrication, corrosion mappingUT Level II or UT knowledge accepted by the written practice
TOFDII, III prepThick-section weld sizing on vessels, heavy-wall piping and heat-recovery equipmentUT Level II
RT (radiographic)I, II, III prepPipeline girth welds, vessel and spool welds for US-code fabrication; film and digital interpretationNone for Level I; CNSC exposure device operator certification is a separate federal legal requirement
MT (magnetic particle)I, II, III prepPipe at integrity digs (including crack detection on in-service lines), structural and module welds, rotating and drilling equipmentNone for Level I
PT (liquid penetrant)I, II, III prepStainless and alloy piping in gas processing and upgrading, castings, non-magnetic componentsNone for Level I
VT (visual)I, II, III prepWeld visual on module, spool and structural fabrication; in-service visual on tanks, vessels and structuresNone for Level I
ET (eddy current)I, II, III prepExchanger and air-cooler tubing at gas plants and in-situ facilities, surface crack detection through coatingsNone for Level I

UT. The course covers ultrasonic physics, calibration, straight-beam thickness and angle-beam weld technique, DAC and TCG, and interpretation against the acceptance criteria of US codes such as ASME Section VIII, B31.3 and API 1104. We also teach temperature effects on velocity and couplant, which matter both for hot in-service piping and for Alberta winter fieldwork.

PAUT and TOFD. These courses cover focal laws, encoded scanning, data analysis and TOFD sizing. Encoded UT is well established on Western Canadian pipeline construction and in module yards, so for a Calgary-based UT technician working on US-code scopes these are high-value additions.

RT. The course covers sources, exposure technique, image quality, and film and digital interpretation of welds. The legal side of radiography in Canada is federal and quite different from the US. It is explained below.

MT and PT. These cover magnetisation methods, wet fluorescent and visible particles, demagnetisation, penetrant methods and dwell times, and interpretation. The courses also cover temperature limits for penetrant procedures and how procedures are qualified for conditions outside them, which is a practical concern in Alberta.

VT. The course covers visual acuity, lighting, gauges and acceptance criteria. Module and spool fabrication for US projects relies on consistent, well-documented weld visual inspection before any volumetric NDT.

ET. The course covers impedance-plane analysis, probe and frequency selection, and tube inspection. Gas plants and in-situ facilities have large exchanger and air-cooler populations.

Level III. Senior technicians who will own SNT-TC-1A written practices for Canadian companies working to US requirements can prepare through our ASNT Level III programme. ASNT administers the Level III exams.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Calgary, step by step

  1. Confirm which scheme the work requires. Before anything else, check the contract, client specification or code. If it calls for CGSB (CAN/CGSB-48.9712), that is a separate national certification with its own requirements. If it calls for SNT-TC-1A, continue with the steps below.
  2. Adopt or update the employer's written practice. The written practice sets training hours, experience, exams, grading and recertification. Many Canadian companies need to create one specifically for their US-code work.
  3. Complete formal training. Classroom hours for the method and level, live online or onsite. Compare the training-requirements matrix with your written practice.
  4. Document on-the-job experience. Supervised experience in the method, logged and signed. Experience gained on CGSB-certified work can often be documented for SNT-TC-1A purposes if the records are good enough, but the written practice decides.
  5. General exam. Written exam on the principles of the method, given under a Level III.
  6. Specific exam. Written exam on the employer's procedures, equipment and the US codes used on the work.
  7. Practical exam. Hands-on exam on specimens with real discontinuities, graded by a Level III.
  8. Vision exam. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast. Near vision is re-checked at least annually.
  9. Employer certification. Written certification by the employer, with the complete file kept for client audits.
  10. Recertification. Follows the written practice interval (SNT-TC-1A recommends a maximum of five years). Technicians who hold both CGSB and SNT-TC-1A certification need to track each scheme's renewal separately.

For the full framework, see SNT-TC-1A training and certification. For how the two approaches compare, see our ISO 9712 vs SNT-TC-1A comparison.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Calgary crews

  • Live online theory. Instructor-led virtual sessions scheduled in Mountain Time, so Calgary technicians can join from home, the office or a camp with reliable connectivity. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility. Practical training and exams at your Calgary shop, module yard or field facility, on your instruments and specimens representative of your US-code scope. This is the usual model for inspection companies and fabricators.
  • Blended. Online theory, then a concentrated onsite practical block.

Alberta's calendar matters. Pipeline construction and integrity digs follow seasonal windows, often shaped by ground conditions and spring road bans. Gas plants and oil-sands facilities run planned turnarounds that absorb inspection crews for weeks. Many fabrication yards are busiest when module deliveries are due. We schedule theory during quieter periods and hold practicals indoors when outdoor conditions rule them out. For larger or multi-site programmes, see corporate NDT training.

The practical exam is always hands-on. Ask about onsite training for your Calgary crew.

Where NDT technicians work in Calgary

Head offices and engineering. Calgary houses the head offices and engineering teams of many of Canada's producers, pipeline companies and midstream operators. They write integrity programmes, select inspection contractors and set qualification requirements. Much of the field work they manage happens elsewhere in Alberta and beyond, but technicians, Level IIIs and integrity specialists based in Calgary support it.

Pipelines. Alberta has a dense network of gathering, feeder and transmission pipelines. Pipelines within Alberta are regulated by the Alberta Energy Regulator (AER). Interprovincial and international pipelines fall under the federal Canada Energy Regulator (CER). Canadian pipelines are designed, built and maintained to CSA Z662, which has its own NDT and personnel provisions. Cross-border systems and US-owned assets may also apply API 1104 and US operator specifications. That is where SNT-TC-1A-qualified personnel are most often required.

Gas processing and in-situ oil sands. Sour-gas processing plants in the foothills and in-situ oil-sands facilities (SAGD) in northeast Alberta are inspected throughout their lives: UT thickness and corrosion mapping, PT on alloy piping, ET on exchangers, and MT and VT on structures and welds.

Pressure equipment. In Alberta, boilers and pressure vessels come under the Alberta Boilers Safety Association (ABSA), which administers the province's pressure-equipment safety legislation, design registration and owner-user programmes. Equipment is registered to CSA B51, and construction is typically to ASME codes. ABSA's requirements are about equipment and quality programmes. They do not decide which NDT personnel scheme applies to your technicians. That comes from the contract, the code edition and the quality programme.

Module and spool fabrication. Alberta's fabrication shops and module yards, in Calgary's industrial districts and along the Edmonton corridor, build piping spools, pressure vessels and process modules for Canadian and US projects. Structural welding in Canada follows CSA W59 and Canadian Welding Bureau certification for fabricators. When products are built to ASME for US installation, clients often require NDE personnel qualified to SNT-TC-1A written practices, which is where our training and written-practice work fits.

Power and aviation. Gas-fired generating stations in and around Calgary need outage NDT on high-energy piping, boilers and heat-recovery steam generators. Aircraft maintenance at Calgary International Airport is governed by Transport Canada, and aviation NDT follows the aviation sector's own qualification requirements, not general industrial practice.

Radiography licensing in Canada. Radiography regulation in Canada is federal. The Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC) licenses companies that possess and use exposure devices (gamma cameras). Anyone operating an exposure device must be a CNSC-certified exposure device operator (EDO) or work under the direct supervision of one. EDO certification involves a recognised vocational training course, supervised on-the-job training with a licensed company, and written and practical exams, as set out by the CNSC. Atlantis does not provide EDO training. Neither SNT-TC-1A RT certification nor CGSB RT certification authorises anyone to operate a camera. They cover technique and interpretation, and EDO certification is a separate legal requirement.

What Calgary employers ask for. For most purely Canadian work, postings ask for CGSB certification in the relevant method, plus EDO certification for radiography. For US-connected work (US clients, cross-border pipelines, ASME fabrication for export, or crews travelling to US sites) they also ask for SNT-TC-1A Level II in UT, PAUT, MT, PT or RT. Some roles also list API 510, 570 or 653 inspector certifications or CWB inspector qualifications. Those are separate schemes that Atlantis does not train. For pay information, see our NDT salary guide.

Level III services and written practices for Calgary NDT companies

Canadian inspection companies and fabricators often run into SNT-TC-1A for the first time when they win a US-client contract or a US-code fabrication order. Their technicians may hold CGSB certification, but the client's specification asks for a written practice, SNT-TC-1A certification records and Level III approval of procedures. Atlantis supports these companies with the following:

  • Written-practice development. An SNT-TC-1A written practice for the methods and levels needed on the US-code scope, drafted so it sits alongside your existing CGSB arrangements. See NDT written practice development.
  • Outsourced ASNT Level III. Exam administration, procedure and technique approval, and certification-file review to support client audits.
  • Dual-scheme record keeping. Advice on keeping CGSB and SNT-TC-1A records separate and consistent, so neither scheme's audit trail is compromised.
  • SNT-TC-1A guidance. SNT-TC-1A certification explains the employer-based model for Canadian managers used to central certification.

Book a Level III consultation and tell us the contract or code requirement you need to meet, the methods and the number of technicians.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Calgary technicians, the oil and gas site, workshop and tank scenarios are closest to daily work. The simulator is useful for rehearsing set-ups and indication recognition between sessions.

It is a practice tool only. It does not replace hands-on training on real instruments, the practical exam on real specimens, or any CGSB or CNSC requirement.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content, exams and practical assessments. Onsite programmes for Calgary employers run under that ASNT Level III oversight.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Calgary

How do I get NDT certified in Calgary?

It depends on the scheme your employer or client needs. For Canadian national certification, the route is CGSB (CAN/CGSB-48.9712), which Atlantis does not provide. For SNT-TC-1A, which is used on US-connected work, your employer certifies you after formal training, documented experience, general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and a vision test. Atlantis provides that training and the written-practice support.

Is ASNT certification recognised in Alberta?

It is accepted where the contract, client or code calls for it, which is common for US-owned operators, cross-border projects and ASME fabrication for US installation. For much purely Canadian work, employers and owners expect CGSB certification. Check what your target employer requires before you train.

Does Atlantis training count toward CGSB certification?

We do not claim it does. CGSB certification has its own training, experience and examination requirements administered through the national scheme. Our training is SNT-TC-1A-based.

Can I take NDT training online in Alberta?

Yes, for theory. Live online sessions run in Mountain Time. Practical training and exams must be done hands-on, onsite at your employer's facility. See online NDT training.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

Under SNT-TC-1A, it depends on your employer's written practice and your starting point. Recommended minimum training and experience hours are in our training-requirements matrix. CGSB requirements are separate and different.

Do I need a licence for radiography in Alberta?

Yes, federally. The Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission licenses companies using exposure devices, and anyone operating one must be a CNSC-certified exposure device operator or work under the direct supervision of one. SNT-TC-1A or CGSB RT certification covers technique and interpretation only.

What does NDT training cost in Calgary?

We do not publish prices. The cost depends on method, level, group size and whether delivery is online, onsite or blended. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day. Request a Calgary training quote.

I want to work on US jobs from Calgary. What do I need?

Most US employers and clients expect SNT-TC-1A certification under their written practice, plus any site or pipeline-specific requirements. Work authorisation for the US is a separate matter entirely. Training in the method gives you the technical foundation.

Can a technician hold both CGSB and SNT-TC-1A certification?

Yes. Many Canadian technicians working cross-border hold both. The two schemes keep separate records and renew on separate schedules.

Can you train our crew onsite in Calgary?

Yes. Onsite delivery at your facility is our standard model for crews. Ask about onsite training for your Calgary crew.

We need an SNT-TC-1A written practice for a US contract. Can you help?

Yes. We develop SNT-TC-1A written practices and provide outsourced ASNT Level III services. See written practice development.

How should I prepare for the practical exam?

Study the method theory, use mock exams such as our UT Level 2 practice questions, and rehearse on the Practical NDT simulator before the hands-on practical.
